You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

such as *\"equal to or better than,\"* *\"at least equal to,\"* or *\"no less favorable than.\"* These formulations impose a floor that ratchets upward and does not permit any reduction or variation, however reasonable.
>
> • **Reject \"Best Practices\" and Similar Standards:** References to *\"industry best practices,\"* *\"commercially reasonable best efforts,\"* or other aspirational benchmarks must be rejected. These terms are undefined, subjective, invite disputes, and impose a standard that may materially exceed what Polaris historically provided to the divested business. Polaris is not a third-party service provider competing for business --- it is providing transitional support as an accommodation.
>
> • **Not a Guarantor:** Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to making available the same general type and level of resources as historically deployed. Service Provider does not guarantee specific outcomes, results, or service levels beyond what was historically provided.
>
> • **APA Precedence:** If the APA specifies a service standard (e.g., in the TSA covenant section or an exhibit), that APA standard controls and the TSA cannot impose a more stringent requirement.

**[2.2 Exclusions from Service Obligation]{.underline}**

Service Provider has no obligation to:

> • **(a)** Provide services not described in the applicable Service Schedules;
>
> • **(b)** Hire additional personnel or acquire additional resources beyond those in place as of the Closing Date;
>
> • **(c)** Provide services that would violate applicable law or regulation;
>
> • **(d)** Provide services that would breach any third-party agreement to which Polaris is a party (including software licenses, vendor contracts, or confidentiality agreements);
>
> • **(e)** Provide advice of any kind --- legal, tax, financial, or strategic.

Service Provider may modify the manner of delivering services to the extent such modifications are consistent with changes made to services provided to Polaris\'s own businesses (e.g., system upgrades, vendor changes, process improvements applied company-wide).

**[Section 3: Term and Termination]{.underline}**

**[3.1 Maximum Term]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Fixed term not to exceed **18 months** from the Closing Date. Hard stop. No automatic renewal. Extensions require: (i) mutual written agreement, (ii) pricing at cost-plus-15%, (iii) maximum extension of 6 months (total possible term: 24 months only upon mutual agreement).

  **Fallback**                        Mutual written extension option at cost-plus-10% (minimum). Never accept automatic renewals.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • The 18-month maximum is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12 in standard Polaris deals. The TSA cannot exceed the APA-mandated term.
>
> • **Automatic renewal provisions are strictly prohibited.** Automatic renewals create open-ended service obligations, may violate APA term caps, deprive Polaris of the ability to reallocate resources to its remaining businesses, and eliminate Polaris\'s leverage to negotiate extension pricing.
>
> • Extension pricing at cost-plus-15% reflects the additional administrative burden, resource diversion, and opportunity cost of extended service delivery beyond the original contemplated term.

**[3.2 Termination of Individual Services]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Either party may terminate any individual Service upon **90 days\'** prior written notice.

  **Fallback**                        90 days for Service Recipient termination; 60 days for Service Provider termination upon Service Recipient material breach. Service Recipient may terminate on 30 days\' notice if the applicable function has been fully migrated.
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The 90-day notice period is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(c). Do not accept termination notice periods longer than 90 days, as longer periods lock Polaris into service obligations even when continued provision is inefficient or undesirable.

**[3.3 Termination for Cause]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Either party may terminate the entire TSA upon material breach if the breaching party fails to cure within **30 days** of receiving written notice. Service Provider may terminate immediately (no cure period) upon: (i) Service Recipient insolvency or bankruptcy, (ii) failure to pay undisputed invoices for more than 60 days past due, or (iii) conduct creating material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk for Polaris.

  **Fallback**                        Accept 45-day cure period. Maintain immediate termination rights for insolvency and non-payment.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[3.4 Termination Assistance / Wind-Down]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Upon expiration or termination of any Service, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for a period not to exceed **60 days** at **cost-plus-15%**. Assistance includes: knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with replacement providers, and transition documentation. No obligation to provide termination assistance if Service Recipient has outstanding unpaid invoices.

  **Fallback**                        Extend termination assistance period to 90 days maximum. Accept cost-plus-10% as absolute floor.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include termination assistance provisions. A TSA that is silent on wind-down obligations creates ambiguity regarding Polaris\'s post-termination cooperation obligations and exposes Polaris to claims that implied duties of good faith require indefinite assistance. Affirmatively negotiating a defined, compensated wind-down period protects Polaris by establishing clear boundaries.

**[Section 4: Service Fees and Payment]{.underline}**

**[4.1 Fee Calculation Methodology]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          All service fees calculated on a **cost-plus-10%** basis: fully-loaded cost (direct labor, allocated overhead, system costs, out-of-pocket expenses) plus a **uniform 10% markup** across all service categories.

  **Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-7% or cost-plus-8% if buyer pushes back. Never accept a markup below cost-plus-5%.
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • The cost-plus-10% cap is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(b). All fee calculations must be verified for compliance with this APA-mandated ceiling.
>
> • The 10% markup applies **uniformly** to all service categories. There shall be no service category that carries a different (higher or lower) markup percentage. Any deviation from uniform pricing must be flagged.
>
> • Each Service Schedule must include: (i) base cost components, (ii) estimated monthly cost, (iii) markup percentage, and (iv) resulting monthly fee. A consolidated Fee Schedule should be attached as an exhibit.

**[4.2 Fee Escalation]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Annual escalation (on each anniversary of Closing) by the greater of **(a) 3%** or **(b) CPI-U** for the trailing 12-month period. Additional escalation upon an \"Escalation Event\" (material cost increase due to changes in law/regulation/vendor pricing, or Service Recipient request for material volume/scope increase).

  **Fallback**                        Accept CPI-U only (no 3% floor). Maintain Escalation Event provision.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[4.3 Payment Terms]{.underline}**

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Monthly invoicing within 15 business days after month-end. Payment due **Net 30** from date of invoice. Late interest at the lesser of **1.5% per month** or maximum rate permitted by law. Undisputed portions must be paid regardless of disputes over other portions.

  **Fallback**                        Accept Net 45 as maximum. Interest at 1.0%/month as floor.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** Never accept vague payment language such as *\"payment within a commercially reasonable time\"* or *\"payment to be made promptly.\"* Specific payment terms are essential for cash flow management and enforcement. Vague formulations are unenforceable as a practical matter and create unnecessary disputes.

**[4.4 Change Orders]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Any request for out-of-scope services, material volume increase, or material scope change requires a **written change order** signed by authorized representatives of both parties. Change order pricing: **cost-plus-15%**. Acceptance at Service Provider\'s **sole discretion**. No obligation to perform until change order is fully executed and any required advance payment received.

  **Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-10% for change orders. Maintain written change order requirement, dual signature, and Service Provider discretion.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include a formal change order procedure. Without one, Service Recipient can expand scope through informal requests and then argue that expanded services are covered under the existing fee structure. A documented change order process protects Polaris against scope creep and ensures compensation for incremental burden.

**[Section 5: Liability and Indemnification]{.underline}**

**[5.1 Limitation of Liability --- Aggregate Cap]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Service Provider\'s aggregate liability shall not exceed total fees actually paid during the **trailing twelve (12) month period** preceding the date on which the claim first arose.

  **Fallback**                        **APA-mandated; not subject to negotiation.** APA Section 7.12(d) specifies the trailing 12-month fee cap. The TSA must conform.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points --- Illustrative Exposure Analysis:**

The distinction between a trailing 12-month fee cap and a total-fees (or total-fee-multiple) cap is significant. Using representative assumptions:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Cap Formulation**                  **Calculation**                **Approximate Exposure**
  ------------------------------------ ------------------------------ --------------------------
  Trailing 12-month fees               \~\$1,122,000/month × 12       **\~\$13,464,000**

  200% of total fees (18-month term)   \~\$1,122,000/month × 18 × 2   **\~\$40,392,000**
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The total-fees formulation creates approximately three times the exposure of the trailing 12-month cap. Reject any liability cap based on total fees paid over the entire term, any multiple thereof, or any fixed dollar amount that exceeds the trailing 12-month fee calculation. The trailing 12-month structure is appropriately calibrated to the ongoing relationship and reflects the APA mandate.

**[5.2 Consequential Damages Waiver]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          **MUTUAL** waiver of all consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages (including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, and diminution in value). Exceptions: (i) breaches of confidentiality, (ii) IP infringement, (iii) third-party claim indemnification.

  **Fallback**                        Firm position. Accept narrow additional carve-outs (willful misconduct, fraud). **Never accept a non-mutual waiver.**
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** The waiver must be **mutual** --- both parties waive claims against the other. A unilateral waiver (where only Service Recipient waives) is insufficient because it leaves Service Provider exposed to potentially unlimited consequential damages claims. As service provider, Polaris\'s consequential damages exposure (e.g., claims for business interruption, lost contracts, or supply chain disruption) could vastly exceed the TSA fee value. The mutual waiver limits both parties to direct damages.

**Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**

At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.

The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.

**Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**

All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.

The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.

Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.

WHEREAS**, Polaris and Trident entered into that certain Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of March 14, 2025 (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"**Purchase Agreement**\" or \"**APA**\"), pursuant to which Polaris agreed to sell, transfer, convey, and deliver to Trident substantially all of the assets of Polaris\'s Specialty Coatings Division (the \"**Business**\") for aggregate consideration of Four Hundred Eighty-Five Million Dollars (\$485,000,000), subject to customary purchase price adjustments;

**WHEREAS**, the Purchase Agreement contemplates that the Parties will enter into this Agreement at or prior to the Closing (as defined in the APA) in order to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Trident and to ensure the continued and uninterrupted provision of certain shared services to the Business during the transition period;

**WHEREAS**, Section 7.12 of the Purchase Agreement requires the Parties to execute and deliver a transition services agreement on \"commercially reasonable terms\" setting forth the terms and conditions upon which Polaris will continue to provide certain shared services to the Business following the Closing;

**WHEREAS**, the Business includes manufacturing facilities located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; Greenville, South Carolina; and Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico, and approximately one thousand one hundred eighty (1,180) employees of the Business will transfer to Trident at the Closing as Transferred Employees in accordance with the terms of the Purchase Agreement; and

**WHEREAS**, Polaris currently provides certain shared services to the Business through its corporate and shared-services organization, utilizing approximately one hundred (100) shared-services personnel who also support other Polaris divisions and business units, and the Parties wish to ensure continuity and stability of such services to the Business during the period following the Closing in which Trident develops and implements its own standalone capabilities.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1** *Defined Terms.* As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Purchase Agreement.

\"**Affiliate**\" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly, through one or more intermediaries, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Person. For purposes of this definition, \"control\" (including the terms \"controlled by\" and \"under common control with\") means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise.
\"**Agreement**\" has the meaning set forth in the preamble.

\"**APA**\" or \"**Purchase Agreement**\" means that certain Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of March 14, 2025, by and between Polaris and Trident, as the same may be amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time in accordance with its terms.

\"**Applicable Law**\" means, with respect to any Person, any federal, state, local, municipal, foreign, international, or multinational law (including common law), statute, constitution, treaty, convention, ordinance, code, rule, regulation, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, directive, guidance, or other similar requirement enacted, adopted, promulgated, or applied by a Governmental Authority that is binding upon or applicable to such Person, as amended unless expressly specified otherwise.
\"**Business**\" means the Specialty Coatings Division of Polaris, as further described in the APA.

\"**Business Day**\" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, or a day on which banking institutions in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, or Cleveland, Ohio, are authorized or required by Applicable Law to close.

\"**Change in Law**\" means any change in, or enactment or promulgation of, any Applicable Law (or any binding interpretation thereof by a Governmental Authority) after the Effective Date that materially affects a Party\'s obligations or rights under this Agreement.
\"**Closing**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in the APA, and is expected to occur on or about June 2, 2025.
\"**Closing Date**\" means the date on which the Closing actually occurs.

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all information, whether written, oral, electronic, or in any other form, that is disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, including business plans, financial data, customer lists, pricing information, technical data, trade secrets, know-how, inventions, processes, software, marketing strategies, and any other proprietary or confidential information of the Disclosing Party. Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the Receiving Party; (b) was already known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (c) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information; or (d) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.
\"**Effective Date**\" means the Closing Date.

\"**ERP System**\" or \"**SAP System**\" means Polaris\'s SAP S/4HANA enterprise resource planning system, including all modules, configurations, customizations, and related infrastructure used in connection with the Business.
\"**Fee Schedule**\" means Schedule G attached hereto, as the same may be amended from time to time in accordance with this Agreement.

289: **[ARTICLE 2 --- SERVICES]{.underline}**
290: 
291: **Section 2.1** *Provision of Services.* Commencing on the Effective Date and continuing during the Term, Service Provider shall provide, or shall cause its Affiliates or designees to provide, to Service Recipient the Services described in the following Schedules:
292: 
293: > \(a\) **Schedule A** --- Financial Reporting & Accounting Services;
294: >
295: > \(b\) **Schedule B** --- Information Technology Services;
296: >
297: > \(c\) **Schedule C** --- Human Resources Services;
298: >
299: > \(d\) **Schedule D** --- Supply Chain & Procurement Services;
300: >
301: > \(e\) **Schedule E** --- Regulatory & EHS Compliance Services; and
302: >
303: > \(f\) **Schedule F** --- Treasury & Tax Services.
304: 
305: The six (6) service categories set forth above correspond to the service categories identified in Exhibit H to the Purchase Agreement. The Services will be provided by an aggregate of approximately one hundred (100) full-time equivalent Service Provider personnel allocated across the service categories as follows: twenty-two (22) FTEs for Financial Reporting & Accounting; thirty-one (31) FTEs for Information Technology; eighteen (18) FTEs for Human Resources; fourteen (14) FTEs for Supply Chain & Procurement; eight (8) FTEs for Regulatory & EHS Compliance; and seven (7) FTEs for Treasury & Tax. The specific scope, deliverables, personnel, systems, and migration milestones for each Service category are set forth in the applicable Schedule. In the event of any conflict between the terms of an individual Schedule and the terms of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Schedule expressly and specifically provides otherwise.
306: 
307: **Section 2.2** *Scope Limitations.* The Services to be provided by Service Provider under this Agreement are limited solely and exclusively to those services expressly described in Schedules A through F. Service Provider shall not be obligated to provide any service or perform any function that is not expressly described in the applicable Schedule. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Service Provider shall not be obligated to: (a) hire additional employees or engage additional contractors solely for the purpose of providing the Services; (b) acquire, lease, or license additional equipment, software, or other assets solely for the purpose of providing the Services; (c) maintain any third-party software license, service contract, or other agreement beyond its current term or renewal period solely for the purpose of providing the Services; or (d) make any capital expenditure solely for the purpose of providing the Services. The scope of each Service is as described in the applicable Schedule as of the Effective Date, and no expansion, modification, or enhancement of any Service shall be required of Service Provider except as may be mutually agreed in writing by the Parties.
308: 
309: **Section 2.3** *Exclusive Remedy.* Service Recipient\'s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Service Provider to perform any of the Services in accordance with this Agreement shall be as expressly set forth in Article 9 (Indemnification) and Article 10 (Limitation of Liability). Service Recipient shall have no other right or remedy at law or in equity with respect to any such failure, except as expressly set forth herein.
310: 
311: **Section 2.4** *Subcontracting.* Service Provider may, in its sole discretion, subcontract or delegate any or all of the Services to qualified third-party subcontractors or to Affiliates of Service Provider; provided that Service Provider shall remain fully responsible for the performance of any subcontracted or delegated Services and for the acts and omissions of any such subcontractor or Affiliate to the same extent as if Service Provider had performed such Services directly. Service Provider shall ensure that any subcontractor or Affiliate performing Services is bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 8.
312: 
313: **[ARTICLE 3 --- SERVICE STANDARDS]{.underline}**
314: 
315: **Section 3.1** *Standard of Performance.* Service Provider shall perform, or cause to be performed, each of the Services at a level of quality, timeliness, and competence at least equal to or better than the level at which such services were provided to the Business during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to the Closing Date, and in all cases in accordance with industry best practices applicable to each such Service (the \"**Service Standard**\"). Service Provider shall allocate sufficient resources, including qualified personnel and appropriate systems, to meet the Service Standard at all times during the Term. In the event of any dispute regarding the Service Standard, the Parties shall refer the matter to the Steering Committee for resolution in accordance with Article 4.
316: 
317: **Section 3.2** *No Guarantee of Results.* Notwithstanding Section 3.1 or any other provision of this Agreement, Service Provider does not guarantee any particular outcome, result, or deliverable from the provision of the Services. Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to performing the Services in accordance with the Service Standard, and Service Provider shall not be liable for any failure to achieve a particular business outcome or result so long as the Services are performed in accordance with the Service Standard.
318: 
319: **Section 3.3** *Cooperation.* Service Recipient shall cooperate with Service Provider and shall provide, in a timely manner, all information, data, access, approvals, decisions, and assistance reasonably necessary for Service Provider to perform the Services in accordance with this Agreement. Service Recipient acknowledges and agrees that Service Provider\'s ability to meet the Service Standard may be materially and adversely affected by Service Recipient\'s failure to cooperate or to provide timely information, access, or decisions as contemplated by this Section 3.3. Service Provider shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performing the Services to the extent such failure or delay is attributable to Service Recipient\'s failure to comply with this Section 3.3.
320: 
321: **[ARTICLE 4 --- GOVERNANCE]{.underline}**
322: 
323: **Section 4.1** *Steering Committee.* Within ten (10) Business Days of the Effective Date, each Party shall designate two (2) senior representatives to serve on a joint transition steering committee (the \"**Steering Committee**\"). The initial designees of the Steering Committee shall be as follows:
324: 
325: > \(a\) **For Service Provider (Polaris):**
326: >
327: > \(i\) David K. Okafor, Chief Financial Officer; and
328: >
329: > \(ii\) Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel.
330: >
331: > \(b\) **For Service Recipient (Trident):**
332: >
333: > \(i\) Patricia N. Suresh, Chief Financial Officer; and
334: >
335: > \(ii\) Robert F. Collier, General Counsel.
336: 
337: Either Party may replace its designees on the Steering Committee at any time upon written notice to the other Party; provided that any replacement designee shall be a senior officer of the designating Party with sufficient authority to make decisions on behalf of such Party with respect to matters arising under this Agreement. The Steering Committee shall meet at least once per calendar month (or more frequently as mutually agreed or as circumstances require) to review and discuss the status of service delivery, migration milestones, key performance metrics, open issues, and any disputes or concerns raised by either Party. Meetings may be held in person or by video or telephone conference. Each Party shall bear its own costs associated with participation in the Steering Committee. The Steering Committee shall not have the authority to amend, modify, or waive any provision of this Agreement, which may be done only in accordance with Section 15.6.
338: 
339: **Section 4.2** *Service Managers.* In addition to its Steering Committee designees, each Party shall designate a Service Manager for each Service category (each, a \"**Service Manager**\") who shall serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day operational matters relating to such Service category. Each Service Manager shall be an individual with relevant operational expertise and sufficient authority to manage day-to-day decisions within the scope of the applicable Service category. Service Managers shall report regularly to the Steering Committee and shall escalate to the Steering Committee any issues that cannot be resolved at the operational level within a reasonable period of time. Each Party shall notify the other Party in writing of the identity and contact information of its Service Managers within five (5) Business Days of the Effective Date.
340: 
341: **Section 4.3** *Key Personnel.* Service Provider shall ensure that the individuals identified on Schedule H attached hereto (the \"**Key Personnel**\") are assigned to perform the Services during the Term at the FTE allocation levels set forth on Schedule H. Service Provider shall not reassign, transfer, terminate (other than for cause as determined by Service Provider in its reasonable judgment), or otherwise remove any Key Personnel from the performance of the Services without the prior written consent of Service Recipient, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. In the event that any Key Personnel individual voluntarily resigns, becomes permanently disabled, or is terminated for cause, Service Provider shall promptly notify Service Recipient and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to replace such individual with a person of substantially similar qualifications, experience, and skill within thirty (30) days, subject to Service Recipient\'s prior written approval of the replacement (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). Service Provider acknowledges that the Key Personnel possess specialized knowledge of the Business and that their continued involvement is material to the successful transition of the Business to Service Recipient.
342: 
343: **Section 4.4** *Reporting.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient, within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, a written report summarizing the Services performed during such month (each, a \"**Monthly Report**\"). Each Monthly Report shall include, at a minimum: (a) hours worked by each FTE assigned to the Services, broken down by Service category; (b) a summary of any material issues, disruptions, or failures in service delivery; (c) a status update on migration milestones, including any variances from the milestone schedule set forth in the applicable Schedule; and (d) such other information as the Steering Committee may reasonably request from time to time.
344: 
345: **[ARTICLE 5 --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**
346: 
347: **Section 5.1** *Initial Term.* This Agreement shall become effective on the Closing Date and shall continue for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Initial Term**\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 5. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall have no force or effect unless and until the Closing occurs under the Purchase Agreement.
348: 
349: **Section 5.2** *Automatic Renewal.* Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).
350: 
351: **Section 5.3** *Termination of Individual Services.* Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of any individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.
352: 
353: **Section 5.4** *Termination for Cause.* Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the breach is of such a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be deemed in default so long as it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; provided, however, that no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days from the date of the initial notice of breach.
354: 
355: **Section 5.5** *Effect of Termination.* Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):
356: 
357: > \(a\) Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease as of the effective date of such termination or expiration;
358: >
359: > \(b\) Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider all accrued but unpaid Fees and expenses for Services actually performed through the effective date of termination or expiration, which payment shall be made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration;
360: >
361: > \(c\) each Party shall promptly return to the other Party, or at the other Party\'s election destroy and certify in writing the destruction of, all Confidential Information of the other Party that relates to the terminated or expired Services, except to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Law or bona fide document retention policies (in which case such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Article 8); and
362: >
363: > \(d\) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services shall cease, except as expressly provided in Section 5.6 (Survival).
364: 
365: **Section 5.6** *Survival.* The provisions of Article 1 (Definitions), Article 7 (Intellectual Property), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Indemnification), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Representations and Warranties), Article 13 (Insurance), Article 14 (Audit Rights), and Article 15 (General Provisions) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with their respective terms.
366: 
367: **[ARTICLE 6 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
368: 
369: **Section 6.1** *Service Charges.* In consideration for the provision of the Services, Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule (Schedule G) for each Service during the Term. The Fees for each Service category are calculated on a cost-plus basis reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service (including personnel costs, allocated overhead, and systems costs), plus a markup as set forth on the Fee Schedule. The Fees represent the sole compensation to which Service Provider is entitled for the provision of the Services, and Service Provider shall not charge Service Recipient for any internal costs, overhead, or administrative expenses except as expressly reflected in the Fee Schedule.
370: 
371: **Section 6.2** *Invoicing.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient a monthly invoice within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, setting forth in reasonable detail the Services performed during such month, the applicable FTE hours, and the Fees due for such month. Each invoice shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as Service Recipient may reasonably request to verify the accuracy of the amounts invoiced. Invoices shall be delivered to the attention of Service Recipient\'s Service Manager for the applicable Service category, with a copy to Service Recipient\'s Chief Financial Officer.
372: 
373: **Section 6.3** *Payment.* Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider in writing from time to time.
374: 
375: **Section 6.4** *Fee Escalation.* The Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule are fixed for the duration of the Term and shall not be subject to escalation or adjustment, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.
376: 
377: **Section 6.5** *Taxes.* All Fees stated in this Agreement and on the Fee Schedule are exclusive of any applicable sales, use, value-added, goods and services, or similar Taxes (collectively, \"**Transaction Taxes**\"). Service Recipient shall be responsible for and shall pay, or reimburse Service Provider for, all Transaction Taxes imposed on or with respect to the Services, other than Taxes measured by Service Provider\'s net income, capital, or franchise. Service Provider shall separately state any Transaction Taxes on its invoices. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize Transaction Taxes and shall cooperate in good faith with the other Party to obtain any available exemptions or reduced rates for such Taxes.
378: 
379: **Section 6.6** *Disputed Amounts.* If Service Recipient disputes any amount set forth on an invoice in good faith, Service Recipient shall: (a) pay the undisputed portion of such invoice when due in accordance with Section 6.3; (b) provide written notice to Service Provider of the disputed amount, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute, within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the applicable invoice; and (c) work in good faith with Service Provider to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days after such notice. If the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within such thirty (30)-day period, either Party may escalate the matter to the Steering Committee. Pending resolution of any disputed amount, Service Provider shall continue to perform the Services without interruption.
380: 
381: **[ARTICLE 7 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
382: 
383: **Section 7.1** *Service Provider Materials --- License Grant.* Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works of any Service Provider Materials (including any tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, or know-how) developed or utilized by Service Provider in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement. This license shall include the right to sublicense to Service Recipient\'s Affiliates, successors, and assigns, and shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason. For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing license extends to all Service Provider Materials that are used, in whole or in part, in the delivery of any of the Services, regardless of whether such Service Provider Materials were created specifically for the Services or existed prior to the Effective Date and were adapted or applied in the course of service delivery. Nothing in this Section 7.1 shall be construed to transfer ownership of any Service Provider Materials to Service Recipient; Service Provider retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Service Provider Materials, subject to the license granted herein.
384: 
385: **Section 7.2** *Service Recipient Materials.* Service Recipient retains all right, title, and interest in and to any data, materials, information, documents, or other content provided by Service Recipient to Service Provider for purposes of the Services (collectively, \"**Service Recipient Materials**\"). Service Provider shall use the Service Recipient Materials solely for the purpose of performing the Services under this Agreement and for no other purpose. Upon termination or expiration of any Service or this Agreement, Service Provider shall promptly return or, at Service Recipient\'s election, destroy all Service Recipient Materials in its possession or control.
386: 
387: **Section 7.3** *Feedback.* To the extent that Service Recipient provides any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests, recommendations, or other feedback to Service Provider regarding the Service Provider Materials or any other intellectual property of Service Provider (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Service Recipient hereby assigns to Service Provider all right, title, and interest in and to such Feedback and agrees that Service Provider is free to use, disclose, reproduce, license, and otherwise distribute and exploit such Feedback as it sees fit, without obligation or restriction of any kind. Service Recipient acknowledges that this assignment is irrevocable and that no additional consideration is required.
388: 
389: **[ARTICLE 8 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
390: 
391: **Section 8.1** *Confidentiality Obligations.* Each Party agrees to hold the other Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence and to protect such Confidential Information using the same degree of care that it uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care. Neither Party shall disclose the other Party\'s Confidential Information to any Person, except to its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the purpose of performing obligations or exercising rights under this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 8. Each Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 8 by its Representatives. Neither Party shall use the other Party\'s Confidential Information for any purpose other than in connection with the performance of its obligations or the exercise of its rights under this Agreement. Without limiting the foregoing, neither Party shall reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble any Confidential Information of the other Party.
392: 
393: **Section 8.2** *Exceptions.* The obligations set forth in Section 8.1 shall not apply to any information that:
394: 
395: > \(a\) is or becomes publicly available other than as a result of a disclosure by the Receiving Party or its Representatives in breach of this Agreement;
396: >
397: > \(b\) was already known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party;
398: >
399: > \(c\) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party; or
400: >
401: > \(d\) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party who is not, to the Receiving Party\'s knowledge, bound by any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.
402: 
403: In addition, the Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by Applicable Law, regulation, or order of a Governmental Authority, or by the rules and regulations of a stock exchange on which the Receiving Party\'s (or its parent\'s) securities are listed; provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party of such required disclosure so as to enable the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. If a protective order or other remedy is not obtained, the Receiving Party shall disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that it is legally required to disclose and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that confidential treatment will be given to such disclosed information.
404: 
405: **Section 8.3** *Survival of Confidentiality.* The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 8 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years following the effective date of such expiration or termination.
