lines.text: > • **(e)** Maintaining compliance with the terms and constraints set forth in the governing purchase agreement.

This Playbook should always be read in conjunction with the applicable Asset Purchase Agreement (or Stock Purchase Agreement, as applicable). Where the APA mandates specific TSA terms --- including service standard, term, fee cap, or liability structure --- the APA controls and those terms are not subject to further negotiation in the TSA. The Playbook serves as the benchmark against which any buyer\'s draft TSA is evaluated, and any deviation from the positions stated herein should be flagged, analyzed, and escalated as appropriate.
**[Section 2: Service Standard]{.underline}**
**[2.1 Standard of Performance]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Services shall be provided *\"in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality provided to the Business during the twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date.\"* No obligation to exceed historical service levels. No obligation to prioritize Service Recipient over Polaris\'s own internal business needs.
**Fallback**                        Add *\"using commercially reasonable efforts\"* after *\"substantially consistent\"* language. This is the maximum concession.
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • **Lookback Period:** The lookback period is twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date. Do not accept a 24-month or longer lookback period. A longer lookback may capture atypical service levels (e.g., pre-pandemic staffing, special project surges) that are not representative of current operations.

> • **\"Substantially Consistent\" Language:** The operative standard is *\"substantially consistent with,\"* which permits reasonable variation. Reject language such as *\"equal to or better than,\"* *\"at least equal to,\"* or *\"no less favorable than.\"* These formulations impose a floor that ratchets upward and does not permit any reduction or variation, however reasonable.

> • **Reject \"Best Practices\" and Similar Standards:** References to *\"industry best practices,\"* *\"commercially reasonable best efforts,\"* or other aspirational benchmarks must be rejected. These terms are undefined, subjective, invite disputes, and impose a standard that may materially exceed what Polaris historically provided to the divested business. Polaris is not a third-party service provider competing for business --- it is providing transitional support as an accommodation.

> • **Not a Guarantor:** Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to making available the same general type and level of resources as historically deployed. Service Provider does not guarantee specific outcomes, results, or service levels beyond what was historically provided.
> • **APA Precedence:** If the APA specifies a service standard (e.g., in the TSA covenant section or an exhibit), that APA standard controls and the TSA cannot impose a more stringent requirement.
**[2.2 Exclusions from Service Obligation]{.underline}**
Service Provider has no obligation to:
> • **(a)** Provide services not described in the applicable Service Schedules;
> • **(b)** Hire additional personnel or acquire additional resources beyond those in place as of the Closing Date;
> • **(c)** Provide services that would violate applicable law or regulation;
> • **(d)** Provide services that would breach any third-party agreement to which Polaris is a party (including software licenses, vendor contracts, or confidentiality agreements);
> • **(e)** Provide advice of any kind --- legal, tax, financial, or strategic.

Service Provider may modify the manner of delivering services to the extent such modifications are consistent with changes made to services provided to Polaris\'s own businesses (e.g., system upgrades, vendor changes, process improvements applied company-wide).
**[Section 3: Term and Termination]{.underline}**
**[3.1 Maximum Term]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Fixed term not to exceed **18 months** from the Closing Date. Hard stop. No automatic renewal. Extensions require: (i) mutual written agreement, (ii) pricing at cost-plus-15%, (iii) maximum extension of 6 months (total possible term: 24 months only upon mutual agreement).
**Fallback**                        Mutual written extension option at cost-plus-10% (minimum). Never accept automatic renewals.
**Key Negotiation Points:**
> • The 18-month maximum is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12 in standard Polaris deals. The TSA cannot exceed the APA-mandated term.

> • **Automatic renewal provisions are strictly prohibited.** Automatic renewals create open-ended service obligations, may violate APA term caps, deprive Polaris of the ability to reallocate resources to its remaining businesses, and eliminate Polaris\'s leverage to negotiate extension pricing.
> • Extension pricing at cost-plus-15% reflects the additional administrative burden, resource diversion, and opportunity cost of extended service delivery beyond the original contemplated term.
**[3.2 Termination of Individual Services]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Recipient indemnifies Service Provider against all third-party claims arising from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance upon Services, except to the extent caused by Service Provider\'s **gross negligence or willful misconduct**. Service Provider\'s indemnification limited to third-party claims arising from its gross negligence or willful misconduct. All indemnification subject to the aggregate cap in Section 5.1.
**Fallback**                        Accept proportionate fault standard. Maintain gross negligence/willful misconduct threshold for Service Provider indemnification.
**[Section 6: Intellectual Property and Data]{.underline}**
**[6.1 IP Ownership]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          All Service Provider IP (proprietary technology, tools, methodologies, templates, software, systems, know-how, and processes) remains the **sole and exclusive property** of Service Provider. **No license, sublicense, right, or interest** granted to Service Recipient. Access ceases immediately upon expiration or termination.

**Fallback**                        **Firm position. No license grant is acceptable.** If buyer requires specific tools post-transition, address through a separate, independently negotiated license agreement with appropriate restrictions and compensation.
**Key Negotiation Points:**
> • Reject any license grant --- including non-exclusive, limited, or term-limited licenses --- to Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, templates, or know-how.

> • **Specifically reject** language granting *\"perpetual,\" \"irrevocable,\"* or *\"royalty-free\"* licenses. Such language permanently divests Polaris of exclusive control over its proprietary operational IP.
> • Service Recipient receives no right to use, access, copy, modify, reverse engineer, or create derivative works of any Service Provider IP outside of receiving the Services during the Term.

> • Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, and know-how have been developed over decades and are deployed across all four operating divisions. Any license to a buyer could compromise Polaris\'s competitive position and the value of these assets across Polaris\'s entire enterprise.
**[6.2 Data Ownership and Confidentiality]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider Data (all data, databases, and information systems owned or operated by Polaris) remains Polaris\'s confidential property. Buyer Data (data relating exclusively to the divested business, generated after Closing) is owned by Service Recipient. Service Provider will cooperate in transferring Buyer Data upon termination. Service Provider systems (including SAP S/4HANA ERP), network infrastructure, and cybersecurity tools remain Service Provider property.

**Fallback**                        Accept reasonable data separation and migration obligations. Maintain ownership of all pre-Closing data, system-level data, and Service Provider proprietary information.
**[6.3 Cross-Border Data Privacy (Mexico / LFPDPPP)]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Where Services involve processing personal data of individuals in Mexico (e.g., payroll, HR, benefits for the Monterrey facility), the TSA must include LFPDPPP-compliant provisions addressing: (i) data controller/processor allocation (Service Recipient as controller, Service Provider as processor), (ii) data processing agreement or equivalent contractual terms, (iii) cross-border data transfer consent mechanisms (privacy notices and consent from Mexican employees), (iv) data security obligations, and (v) breach notification requirements.

**Fallback**                        At minimum, include a general provision requiring compliance with all applicable data privacy laws, expressly referencing the LFPDPPP, and allocate responsibility for obtaining necessary employee consents.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must not reference only U.S. data privacy laws. Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) imposes distinct requirements including mandatory privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), consent obligations, and cross-border transfer restrictions. Failure to address these requirements in the TSA exposes both parties to enforcement risk by Mexico\'s INAI (*Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Información y Protección de Datos Personales*).
**[Section 7: Personnel]{.underline}**
**[7.1 Staffing Discretion]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider has **sole discretion** over staffing, assignment, reassignment, and replacement of all service-providing personnel, including the right to reassign, promote, transfer, or terminate any individual. Service Provider shall maintain reasonably qualified staff sufficient to meet the applicable service standard.

**Fallback**                        Accept obligation to provide Service Recipient **15 business days\' advance written notice** before reassigning or replacing personnel on a mutually agreed list, together with obligation to assign a reasonably qualified replacement. Reassignment/replacement decisions remain within Service Provider\'s **sole discretion** --- no consent requirement.
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • Do not accept \"Key Personnel\" provisions requiring Service Recipient\'s prior written consent for reassignment or replacement of named individuals. Such provisions undermine Polaris\'s operational flexibility, create potential employment law complications (employees cannot be contractually \"locked\" to a specific assignment by a third party), and give the buyer undue influence over Polaris\'s internal HR decisions.
> • Polaris must retain the ability to manage its workforce across all four divisions without requiring third-party approval.
**[7.2 Non-Solicitation of Service Provider Personnel]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          During the Term and for **12 months** following termination/expiration, Service Recipient shall not solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any Polaris employee who provided Services, without Polaris\'s prior written consent. Applies to all service-providing employees (not limited to any Key Personnel list). Exceptions: (i) general solicitations not targeting Service Provider personnel, (ii) individuals terminated by Service Provider without cause.
**Fallback**                        Reduce post-termination period to 6 months (absolute minimum). Maintain restriction during the Term.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include a non-solicitation covenant. Without one, the buyer can cherry-pick Polaris\'s most effective employees --- who gain deep familiarity with the buyer\'s operations through the TSA engagement --- depleting Polaris\'s workforce and undermining both TSA performance and Polaris\'s ability to serve its remaining businesses. This provision is a high-priority negotiation item.
**[Section 8: Insurance]{.underline}**
**[8.1 Service Recipient Insurance Requirements]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Recipient shall maintain throughout the Term (and for 12 months following expiration/termination): (a) **CGL: \$5M per occurrence / \$5M aggregate**; (b) **Umbrella/Excess: \$5M**; (c) **Workers\' Comp: statutory limits**. Service Provider named as **additional insured** under CGL and Umbrella. All policies include **waiver of subrogation** in favor of Service Provider. Certificates of insurance within 10 business days of Closing and annually thereafter.

**Fallback**                        Accept \$3M CGL and \$3M Umbrella as absolute minimums. **Never** accept CGL below \$3M, waive the umbrella requirement, or omit the additional insured endorsement.

Adequate insurance requirements protect Polaris against claims arising from the buyer\'s operations and use of Polaris\'s services and systems. Given the industrial nature of the divested businesses (coatings, chemicals, manufacturing), the risk profile warrants robust coverage. The additional insured endorsement is particularly important as it provides Polaris with direct rights under the buyer\'s policies.
**[Section 9: Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**[9.1 Service Recipient Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**Position**

lines.text: **[Section 9: Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**[9.1 Service Recipient Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**Position**
**Target**                          Service Recipient may audit Service Provider\'s fee-related books and records subject to the following parameters:
**Parameter**              **Target Position**                                                                                                    **Fallback Position**
**Frequency**              Once per 12-month period                                                                                               Twice per TSA term (not twice per calendar year)
**Notice**                 30 business days\' prior written notice                                                                                20 business days\' notice (minimum)
**Timing**                 During Service Provider\'s normal business hours                                                                       Same

**Cost**                   At Service Recipient\'s sole expense                                                                                   Same; never accept audit at Service Provider\'s expense as default
**Scope**                  Fee-related records only; excludes proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, and unrelated personnel records   Same; maintain scope limitations
**Confidentiality**        All audit results confidential; no disclosure to third parties                                                         Same
**Overcharge Threshold**   If overcharge exceeds 5% for audited period, Service Provider reimburses overcharge and reasonable audit costs         Same

**Key Negotiation Points:** Excessive or frequent audits are disruptive to Polaris\'s operations. Requiring Polaris to bear audit costs as a default incentivizes frivolous audits. Short notice periods do not allow adequate preparation time and may result in incomplete responses that are then characterized as non-cooperation.
**[Section 10: Force Majeure]{.underline}**
**[10.1 Force Majeure Events]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Standard force majeure clause excusing nonperformance caused by events beyond reasonable control (natural disasters, pandemics, acts of war/terrorism, government actions, embargoes, sanctions, strikes, power failures, internet/telecom outages, cyberattacks). Affected party must provide prompt notice and use commercially reasonable mitigation efforts. Obligations suspended (not terminated) during the event. **Termination trigger: if force majeure continues for 90+ consecutive days**, either party may terminate affected Service(s) without penalty.
**Fallback**                        Accept 120-day trigger as maximum. **Never agree to a force majeure clause without a termination trigger.**

A force majeure clause without a termination trigger could leave Polaris obligated to resume services indefinitely after the event ends, regardless of how long the interruption lasted or how much circumstances have changed. The termination trigger provides both parties with a defined exit point.
**[Section 11: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
**[11.1 Governing Law]{.underline}**
**Position**
**Target**                          **Commonwealth of Pennsylvania** law, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.
**Fallback**                        Accept **Delaware** law if the APA is governed by Delaware law. Do not accept the Service Recipient\'s home-state law.

Polaris is headquartered in Pittsburgh. The majority of service-providing personnel are Pennsylvania-based. Pennsylvania law is most familiar to Polaris\'s in-house legal team and outside counsel (Whitfield & Crane LLP). Home-state governing law is a standard and reasonable position for the service provider.

**Position**

**Target**                          Three-step process: **(1) Escalation** to designated senior executives (CFO or General Counsel level) --- 15 business day resolution period; **(2) Mediation** (optional, non-binding); **(3) Binding arbitration** administered by **AAA** under Commercial Arbitration Rules, in **Pittsburgh, PA**, before a single arbitrator with relevant industry experience.

**Fallback**                        Accept arbitration in a neutral location (New York or Philadelphia). Accept three-arbitrator panel for disputes exceeding \$5M. **Do not accept litigation as a dispute resolution mechanism.**
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • **Arbitration is strongly preferred over litigation.** Reasons: (a) confidentiality --- TSA disputes involve proprietary service-level and cost information; (b) speed; (c) arbitrators with industry expertise; (d) limited discovery reduces burden on Polaris; (e) Pittsburgh venue is convenient for Polaris\'s personnel and counsel.

> • Do not accept litigation in the buyer\'s home jurisdiction. State-court litigation creates home-court advantage for the buyer, exposes disputes to public dockets, and subjects Polaris to potentially unfavorable local procedural rules.

**Position**

**Target**                          Where the divested business includes a facility operating under Mexico\'s IMMEX program, the TSA must address: (i) allocation of responsibility for maintaining IMMEX certification during the transition (buyer bears primary responsibility as new operator; Polaris may provide specified transition services such as customs brokerage and import/export documentation); (ii) Polaris\'s obligation, if any, to assist with IMMEX certification transfer or renewal; (iii) compliance with all IMMEX requirements (temporary importation of materials, recordkeeping, periodic reporting to Mexico\'s Secretaría de Economía); (iv) liability allocation for IMMEX non-compliance during the transition.

Mutual confidentiality obligations with a three (3) year survival period following expiration or termination.     if tcBorders is None:

def add_memo_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font=7.8):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; t.autofit=False
    if widths:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths): t.columns[i].width=Inches(w)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text=h; set_cell_shading(c,NAVY); set_cell_margins(c,70,80,70,80)
        for p in c.paragraphs:
            for r in p.runs: r.font.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255); r.font.size=Pt(font)
    set_repeat_table_header(t.rows[0])
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text=val; set_cell_margins(cells[i],70,80,70,80); set_cell_border(cells[i],top={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'},bottom={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'},left={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'},right={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'})
            if i==0: set_cell_shading(cells[i], 'EEF3F8')
            for p in cells[i].paragraphs:
                for r in p.runs: r.font.size=Pt(font); r.bold=(i==0)
    return t

def add_memo_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font=7.8):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; t.autofit=False
    if widths:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths): t.columns[i].width=Inches(w)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text=h; set_cell_shading(c,NAVY); set_cell_margins(c,70,80,70,80)
        for p in c.paragraphs:
            for r in p.runs: r.font.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255); r.font.size=Pt(font)
    set_repeat_table_header(t.rows[0])
    for row in rows:

def add_memo_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font=7.8):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; t.autofit=False
    if widths:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths): t.columns[i].width=Inches(w)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text=h; set_cell_shading(c,NAVY); set_cell_margins(c,70,80,70,80)
        for p in c.paragraphs:
            for r in p.runs: r.font.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255); r.font.size=Pt(font)
    set_repeat_table_header(t.rows[0])
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text=val; set_cell_margins(cells[i],70,80,70,80); set_cell_border(cells[i],top={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'},bottom={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'},left={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'},right={'val':'single','sz':'4','color':'D9D9D9'})
            if i==0: set_cell_shading(cells[i], 'EEF3F8')
            for p in cells[i].paragraphs:
                for r in p.runs: r.font.size=Pt(font); r.bold=(i==0)
    return t

lines.text: **WHITFIELD & CRANE LLP**
**SELLER-SIDE TSA MARKUP**
*Annotated redline of Trident draft --- Specialty Coatings divestiture*
Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. / Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc.
**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL\
ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT**
# Markup instructions and legend

**Scope:** This document is a seller-side markup of Trident's April 28, 2025 draft Transition Services Agreement. It is benchmarked against APA §7.12, Exhibit H and the Polaris TSA Playbook (January 15, 2025).

**Redline convention:** Red strike-through text is proposed for deletion. Blue underlined text is proposed insertion. The adjacent shaded box is the seller comment, stating basis, risk if unchanged, and negotiation posture.

**Global drafting direction:** The TSA is an accommodation to facilitate migration, not a long-term managed-services contract. Polaris should preserve operational discretion, require compensation for incremental burden, and make Trident's migration obligations commercially meaningful.
# Executive markup summary

- Critical: conform the service standard, term/renewal, individual-service termination notice, fee mechanics, liability cap, consequential-damages waiver, cross-border provisions and APA precedence to the executed APA.

- Significant: remove the perpetual IP license; restore Polaris staffing discretion; narrow indemnity; add payment, escalation, termination assistance, change orders, non-solicitation, audit protections, insurance, force-majeure exit and Pennsylvania/AAA arbitration.
- Minor: clean up notices, seller representations, schedule-level open-ended requests and best-practice references; align Schedule H with the revised staffing provision.
# Financial exposure snapshot
**Scenario**                          **Draft exposure**   **APA / corrected exposure**   **Delta**
**Monthly fees (all six services)**   \$1,139,000          \$1,122,000                    \$17,000/mo IT overage

Assumptions: all six services run for 18 months; fees are paid as scheduled; the draft's 15% IT markup is unchanged unless corrected. The draft's 200% cap is applied to cumulative fees paid. The APA cap is trailing twelve-month fees actually paid, with the first twelve months calculated from Closing through claim assertion.
# Critical changes --- must conform to APA
## C-1. Section 3.1 --- Service Standard --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| **Draft:** ~~"at least equal to or better than" the service level during the 24-month pre-Closing period and "in all cases" in accordance with industry best practices.~~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | **Basis:** APA §§7.12(a), 7.12(f); Playbook §§2.1--2.2.                                                                                                                                                                   |

| **Proposed:** [Provide the Services in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and quality provided to or on behalf of the Business during the 12 months immediately preceding Closing. Polaris is not required to exceed historical quality, timeliness or responsiveness, prioritize Trident over retained businesses, or adopt new methodologies, systems, standards or best practices not used for the Business during that period.]{.underline} | **Risk:** The draft creates a 24-month ratcheting floor and an external best-practice overlay, turning an accommodation into an outcome-oriented service guarantee and potentially forcing Polaris to prioritize Trident. |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **Position:** Firm / must-change. No compromise on the 12-month lookback or removal of best-practice language.                                                                                                            |
## C-2. Section 5.2 --- Automatic Renewal --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                                                          |

| **Draft:** ~~Automatic six-month renewals, up to two Renewal Terms, unless Polaris gives 120 days' non-renewal notice; fees remain fixed.~~                                                                                                                                                                                           | **Basis:** APA §7.12(a) expressly prohibits automatic renewal and permits only a mutually agreed written extension of an individual service for up to six additional months; Playbook §3.1. |

| **Proposed:** [Delete Section 5.2 in its entirety. The Agreement expires 18 months after Closing. Any extension for an individual Service requires a written amendment signed by both Parties, may not exceed six months beyond the Maximum TSA Term, and is priced at cost-plus-15%. No automatic renewal or extension.]{.underline} | **Risk:** The draft can create a 30-month service relationship by notice failure, contrary to the APA, and leaves Polaris locked into below-market pricing while losing migration leverage. |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **Position:** Firm / must-change. The cost-plus-15% extension price is a seller target; the no-auto-renewal and written-extension requirements are non-negotiable.                          |
## C-3. Section 5.3 --- Termination of Individual Services --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                     |

| **Draft:** ~~Either party may terminate an individual Service on not less than 120 days' notice; fees cease on the termination date.~~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | **Basis:** APA §7.12(c) establishes 90 days as both minimum and maximum; the APA also preserves reimbursement for non-cancelable costs. Playbook §3.2. |

| **Proposed:** [Either Party may terminate an individual Service on exactly 90 days' prior written notice. Trident remains responsible for accrued Fees and reasonable non-cancelable costs or commitments incurred before Polaris received the notice in reasonable reliance on continuation of the Service, subject to Polaris's commercially reasonable mitigation efforts.]{.underline} | **Risk:** A 120-day lock-in exceeds the APA and prolongs inefficient service delivery. The draft also shifts stranded-cost risk to Polaris.            |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | **Position:** Firm / must-change as to 90 days and stranded-cost reimbursement; mitigation language is negotiable.                                     |
## C-4. Section 6.1 and Schedule G --- Fee cap and APA fee mechanics --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| **Draft:** ~~Schedule B / Schedule G charge 15% on Information Technology, producing a \$391,000 monthly IT fee and \$1,139,000 total monthly fees; fees are fixed and there is no APA actual-cost adjustment process.~~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | **Basis:** APA §7.12(b) and Exhibit H. Exhibit H estimates total \$1,020,000 cost and \$1,122,000 monthly fee; the APA expressly permits actual-cost adjustment and separately negotiated Additional Services.                                    |

| **Proposed:** [Apply a uniform 10% markup to every Service category. Correct IT to \$374,000/month and the aggregate to \$1,122,000/month. Add that fees are subject to adjustment to actual Fully-Loaded Costs under APA §7.12(b), with any increase over Exhibit H estimates by more than 5% requiring Buyer consent. Additional Services require a written agreement and may be priced at a mutually agreed markup, including above 10% where expressly agreed.]{.underline} | **Risk:** The 15% IT markup is a direct APA violation and overcharges \$17,000/month (\$306,000 over 18 months if unchanged). Fixed-fee language may prevent Polaris from recovering actual cost increases or properly pricing out-of-scope work. |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | **Position:** Firm / must-change as to the 10% cap and APA mechanics. Flexibility on administrative mechanics, not on the cap.                                                                                                                    |
## C-5. Section 10.1 --- Aggregate Liability Cap --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| **Draft:** ~~Polaris liability capped at 200% of total Service Charges actually paid as of the claim date.~~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | **Basis:** APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.1. The APA cap is a trailing twelve-month paid-fee cap, not a total-fee percentage.                                                                                              |

| **Proposed:** [Polaris's aggregate liability under or in connection with this Agreement is capped at the total TSA Fees actually paid during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the claim is first asserted in writing. During the first 12 months after Closing, the cap is the fees actually paid from Closing through assertion. Exclusions track APA §7.12(d): fraud or willful misconduct; confidentiality breaches; and indemnification obligations for third-party claims to the extent caused by gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct.]{.underline} | **Risk:** At the scheduled draft fees, the draft cap is \$27.336m at month 12 versus \$13.464m under the APA (delta \$13.872m). At month 18, it is \$41.004m versus \$13.464m (delta \$27.540m, approximately 3.05x). |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | **Position:** Firm / must-change. No fixed amount, total-term formula or multiple may replace the APA formulation.                                                                                                    |
## C-6. Section 10.2 --- Consequential Damages --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                                                        |

| **Draft:** ~~Only Service Provider waives consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary and indirect damages against Service Recipient.~~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Basis:** APA §7.12(d) requires a bilateral waiver; Playbook §5.2 makes mutuality a firm position.                                                                                       |

| **Proposed:** [Each Party waives claims against the other for consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary and punitive damages, including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, cost of replacement services, diminution in value and loss of goodwill. The waiver does not limit confidentiality, IP infringement, fraud/willful misconduct, or third-party indemnification claims to the extent expressly carved out in the agreed liability structure.]{.underline} | **Risk:** The one-way waiver leaves Polaris exposed to Trident's potentially outsized consequential-damages claims while depriving Polaris of the reciprocal protection Trident receives. |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | **Position:** Firm / must-change. Mutuality is not negotiable; narrow carve-outs can be discussed.                                                                                        |
## C-7. Section 8.4, Schedule C §6 and Schedule E §6 --- Mexico cross-border compliance --- CRITICAL

| **SELLER REDLINE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **SELLER COMMENT**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| **Draft:** ~~Data privacy clause addresses only U.S. data privacy laws. Monterrey provisions mention Mexican payroll and EHS assistance but do not allocate IMMEX certification/reporting responsibility or establish LFPDPPP processing terms.~~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | **Basis:** APA §7.12(g); Exhibit H Category 3 and Category 5; Playbook §6.3 and §12.                                                                                                                                                                                          |

| **Proposed:** [Add a Mexico addendum / Article 8.4A providing: (i) Trident is the primary operator and controller responsible for employee notices, lawful basis and consents; (ii) Polaris acts only as processor/service provider for specified payroll/HR functions; (iii) compliance with the LFPDPPP and Regulations, including avisos de privacidad, cross-border transfer mechanisms, minimum-necessary processing, security safeguards, subprocessor controls, cooperation and prompt incident notice; and (iv) Trident bears primary responsibility for maintaining or obtaining Monterrey's IMMEX certification, reports and temporary-importation records. Polaris provides only specified, paid transition assistance and is not liable for Trident's post-Closing certification failure. Add notice/escalation obligations for any jeopardy to certification or data security.]{.underline} | **Risk:** IMMEX lapse can cause duties, penalties and operational interruption. LFPDPPP gaps expose Polaris to Mexican privacy enforcement and employee claims for processing / cross-border transfers involving 300+ Mexican employees; the current allocation is ambiguous. |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **Position:** Firm to require substantive coverage.
